claim: Cytoplasmic dynein is the only major retrograde transporter along microtubules.
source: As the only major retrograde transporter along microtubules, cytoplasmic dynein plays crucial roles in the intracellular transport of organelles and other cargoes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about dynein function.

claim: Dynein intermediate chain (IC) binds three dimeric dynein light chains at multivalent sites.
source: Central to the function of this motor protein complex is dynein intermediate chain (IC), which binds the three dimeric dynein light chains at multivalent sites, and dynactin p150Glued and nuclear distribution protein (NudE) at overlapping sites of its intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Dynactin p150Glued and NudE bind IC at overlapping sites in the intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain.
source: Central to the function of this motor protein complex is dynein intermediate chain (IC), which binds the three dimeric dynein light chains at multivalent sites, and dynactin p150Glued and nuclear distribution protein (NudE) at overlapping sites of its intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The disorder in IC has hindered cryo-electron microscopy and X-ray crystallography studies of its structure and interactions.
source: The disorder in IC has hindered cryo-electron microscopy and X-ray crystallography studies of its structure and interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in structural studies of IC.

claim: IC1-260 constructs show a significant reduction in binding affinity to p150Glued compared to short IC constructs.
source: we identify a significant reduction in binding affinity of IC to p150Glued and a loss of binding to NudE for constructs containing the entire N-terminal domain as well as for full-length constructs when compared to the tight binding observed with short IC constructs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ITC data in Figure 6C.

claim: IC1-260 constructs show a loss of binding to NudE compared to short IC constructs.
source: we identify a significant reduction in binding affinity of IC to p150Glued and a loss of binding to NudE for constructs containing the entire N-terminal domain as well as for full-length constructs when compared to the tight binding observed with short IC constructs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ITC data in Figure 6C.

claim: Autoinhibition in IC is caused by long-range intramolecular interactions between the N-terminal single α-helix and residues closer to the end of the N-terminal domain.
source: We attribute this difference to autoinhibition caused by long-range intramolecular interactions between the N-terminal single α-helix of IC, the common site for p150Glued, and NudE binding, and residues closer to the end of the N-terminal domain.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by NMR data in Figure 5.

claim: Autoinhibition in IC is differentially regulated by light chain binding.
source: Reconstitution of IC subcomplexes demonstrates that autoinhibition is differentially regulated by light chains binding, underscoring their importance both in assembly and organization of IC, and in selection between multiple binding partners at the same site.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by AUC and NMR data in Figures 7-9.

claim: Kinesins typically move toward the plus-end of microtubules.
source: Whereas kinesins typically move toward the plus-end of microtubules, dynein moves toward the minus-end.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about motor protein directionality.

claim: Dynein moves toward the minus-end of microtubules.
source: Whereas kinesins typically move toward the plus-end of microtubules, dynein moves toward the minus-end.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about motor protein directionality.

claim: Mutations in the dynein transport machinery have been linked to neurological and neurodevelopmental diseases.
source: Mutations in the dynein transport machinery have been linked to neurological and neurodevelopmental diseases such as Perry syndrome, spinal muscular atrophy-lower extremity predominant, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, lissencephaly, and other malformations of cortical development (Lipka et al., 2013; Harada et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: A single dynein (cytoplasmic dynein-1) performs a wide variety of functions whereas more than 40 kinesins are used to carry out a comparable number of functions.
source: Importantly, a single dynein (cytoplasmic dynein-1) performs a wide variety of functions whereas more than 40 kinesins are used to carry out a comparable number of functions (Reck-Peterson et al., 2018), underscoring dynein's significance and also suggesting a high level of intricate regulation processes that dictate interactions within and between dynein subunits.
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: There are two copies of IC in the dynein motor protein complex.
source: Like all other dynein subunits, there are two copies of IC in the dynein motor protein complex.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about dynein structure.

claim: IC connects the three dynein light chains (Tctex, LC8, and LC7) to the heavy chain.
source: These two IC subunits connect the three dynein light chains (Tctex, LC8, and LC7) to the heavy chain (HC) and serve as the primary binding site of multiple non-dynein proteins essential for dynein regulation, such as the p150Glued subunit of dynactin and nuclear distribution protein (NudE) (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a known function of IC.

claim: IC serves as the primary binding site of p150Glued and NudE.
source: These two IC subunits connect the three dynein light chains (Tctex, LC8, and LC7) to the heavy chain (HC) and serve as the primary binding site of multiple non-dynein proteins essential for dynein regulation, such as the p150Glued subunit of dynactin and nuclear distribution protein (NudE) (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a known function of IC.

claim: The N-terminal domain of IC is intrinsically disordered.
source: The primarily disordered N-terminal domain of IC (N-IC) (Makokha et al., 2002) contains a single α-helix (SAH) and a short helix (H2), each of which is followed by disordered linker regions (Jie et al., 2015), whereas the C-terminal domain (C-IC) consists of seven WD40 repeats that fold into a β-propeller and binds helical bundles 4 and 5 of HC (Urnavicius et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2017; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: The C-terminal domain of IC consists of seven WD40 repeats that fold into a β-propeller.
source: The primarily disordered N-terminal domain of IC (N-IC) (Makokha et al., 2002) contains a single α-helix (SAH) and a short helix (H2), each of which is followed by disordered linker regions (Jie et al., 2015), whereas the C-terminal domain (C-IC) consists of seven WD40 repeats that fold into a β-propeller and binds helical bundles 4 and 5 of HC (Urnavicius et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2017; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: The C-terminal domain of IC binds helical bundles 4 and 5 of the heavy chain.
source: The primarily disordered N-terminal domain of IC (N-IC) (Makokha et al., 2002) contains a single α-helix (SAH) and a short helix (H2), each of which is followed by disordered linker regions (Jie et al., 2015), whereas the C-terminal domain (C-IC) consists of seven WD40 repeats that fold into a β-propeller and binds helical bundles 4 and 5 of HC (Urnavicius et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2017; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: Free N-IC is monomeric.
source: Free N-IC is monomeric but, upon binding the homodimeric dynein light chain subunits (Tctex, LC8, and LC7), it dimerizes to form a subcomplex that is best described as a polybivalent scaffold (Nyarko and Barbar, 2011; Barbar and Nyarko, 2015; Lo et al., 2001; Mok et al., 2001; Susalka et al., 2002; Hall et al., 2010; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: N-IC dimerizes upon binding the homodimeric dynein light chain subunits.
source: Free N-IC is monomeric but, upon binding the homodimeric dynein light chain subunits (Tctex, LC8, and LC7), it dimerizes to form a subcomplex that is best described as a polybivalent scaffold (Nyarko and Barbar, 2011; Barbar and Nyarko, 2015; Lo et al., 2001; Mok et al., 2001; Susalka et al., 2002; Hall et al., 2010; Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: Binding of one light chain to IC results in a 50-fold enhancement in the affinity for binding the other light chain in the IC/Tctex/LC8 complex.
source: Such a mechanism has been well described for the IC/Tctex/LC8 complex, for which a three-residue linker separates the Tctex and LC8 binding sites. In this complex, binding of one light chain to IC results in a 50-fold enhancement in the affinity for binding the other light chain (Hall et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to prior literature.

claim: A three-residue linker separates the Tctex and LC8 binding sites in IC.
source: Such a mechanism has been well described for the IC/Tctex/LC8 complex, for which a three-residue linker separates the Tctex and LC8 binding sites.
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to prior literature.

claim: Dynactin binds dynein with its largest subunit, p150Glued.
source: Dynactin is a multisubunit complex that binds dynein with its largest subunit, p150Glued, and this interaction is required for the recruitment of cargo, dynein processivity, and correct spindle formation in cell division (King et al., 2003; Gill et al., 1991; Kardon and Vale, 2009; Schroer, 2004; Splinter et al., 2012; Carter et al., 2016; Urnavicius et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: The interaction between dynactin and dynein is required for the recruitment of cargo, dynein processivity, and correct spindle formation in cell division.
source: Dynactin is a multisubunit complex that binds dynein with its largest subunit, p150Glued, and this interaction is required for the recruitment of cargo, dynein processivity, and correct spindle formation in cell division (King et al., 2003; Gill et al., 1991; Kardon and Vale, 2009; Schroer, 2004; Splinter et al., 2012; Carter et al., 2016; Urnavicius et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: NudE regulates dynein recruitment to kinetochores and membranes, centrosome migration, mitotic spindle orientation, and binds LIS1.
source: NudE, on the other hand, regulates dynein recruitment to kinetochores and membranes, centrosome migration, mitotic spindle orientation, and binds LIS1 (Lissencephaly-1 homolog) (Kardon and Vale, 2009; Feng and Walsh, 2004; Wainman et al., 2009; Liang et al., 2007; McKenney et al., 2011; Wang and Zheng, 2011; Zyłkiewicz et al., 2011; Yamada et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: The coiled-coil domains of p150Glued and NudE each bind IC at the same site (the SAH region) for homologs from multiple species (rat, Drosophila, yeast).
source: Previously, we showed using homologs from multiple species (rat, Drosophila, yeast) that the coiled-coil domains of p150Glued and NudE each bind IC at the same site (the SAH region) (Morgan et al., 2011; Jie et al., 2017; Nyarko et al., 2012) whereas for homologs from a filamentous fungus (Chaetomium thermophilum [Ct]) the binding of IC and p150Glued also involves binding of the H2 region (Loening et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: For Chaetomium thermophilum homologs, the binding of IC and p150Glued also involves binding of the H2 region.
source: Previously, we showed using homologs from multiple species (rat, Drosophila, yeast) that the coiled-coil domains of p150Glued and NudE each bind IC at the same site (the SAH region) (Morgan et al., 2011; Jie et al., 2017; Nyarko et al., 2012) whereas for homologs from a filamentous fungus (Chaetomium thermophilum [Ct]) the binding of IC and p150Glued also involves binding of the H2 region (Loening et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Dynactin reorients the motor domains of dynein parallel to the microtubules prior to binding.
source: Extensive cryo-EM structure analyses show that dynactin reorients the motor domains of dynein parallel to the microtubules prior to binding (Zhang et al., 2017; Chowdhury et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: Various adaptors can recruit a second dynein to dynactin for faster movement.
source: Additionally, various adaptors can recruit a second dynein to dynactin for faster movement (Urnavicius et al., 2018; Chaaban and Carter, 2022).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: The flexibility of N-IC limits details of its structure and binding interactions in cryo-EM studies.
source: However, a recurring theme in these studies is that the flexibility of N-IC limits details of its structure and binding interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in cryo-EM studies.

claim: Ct IC1-260 is far longer than Ct, Drosophila, and rat constructs that have been previously studied.
source: The Ct IC1-260 (residues 1–260) construct used in this work is far longer than Ct, Drosophila, and rat constructs that we have previously studied (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing construct comparisons.

claim: LC8, LC7, and Tctex have similar sedimentation coefficients in the 2-3 S range.
source: SV-AUC showed that IC1-260, the three light chains, and non-dynein proteins p150CC1B and NudECC all have similar sedimentation coefficients (in the 2–3 S range, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: IC1-260, p150CC1B, and NudECC all have similar sedimentation coefficients in the 2-3 S range.
source: SV-AUC showed that IC1-260, the three light chains, and non-dynein proteins p150CC1B and NudECC all have similar sedimentation coefficients (in the 2–3 S range, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: All proteins (IC1-260, light chains, p150CC1B, NudECC) show a single sharp peak in the c(s) distribution, indicating that they are homogeneous in solution.
source: Furthermore, all proteins show a single sharp peak in the c(s) distribution, indicating that they are homogeneous in solution.
evidence: This is stated based on SV-AUC data interpretation.

claim: p150CC1B and NudECC have smaller sedimentation coefficients than would typically be expected for globular proteins with their respective dimeric masses.
source: In comparison to the sedimentation coefficients for IC1-260 and the light chains, both p150CC1B and NudECC have smaller sedimentation coefficients than would typically be expected for globular proteins with their respective dimeric masses.
evidence: This is stated based on SV-AUC data interpretation.

claim: The smaller sedimentation coefficients observed for p150CC1B and NudECC are consistent with their predicted coiled-coil structures causing slower sedimentation than if they were globular.
source: However, as sedimentation coefficients also depend on shape, the smaller values observed for p150CC1B and NudECC are consistent with their predicted coiled-coil structures (which result in elongated, less-compact, rod-like shapes), causing slower sedimentation than if they were globular.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the SV-AUC data.

claim: SE-AUC data fit to a monomer-dimer model with dimerization dissociation constants of 0.03 μM and 0.20 μM for p150CC1B and NudECC, respectively.
source: SE-AUC data fit to a monomer-dimer model with dimerization dissociation constants of 0.03 μM and 0.20 μM for p150CC1B and NudECC, respectively, indicate that both are strong dimers and that, of the two, p150CC1B is the tighter dimer (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: Both p150CC1B and NudECC are strong dimers.
source: SE-AUC data fit to a monomer-dimer model with dimerization dissociation constants of 0.03 μM and 0.20 μM for p150CC1B and NudECC, respectively, indicate that both are strong dimers and that, of the two, p150CC1B is the tighter dimer (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: p150CC1B is a tighter dimer than NudECC.
source: SE-AUC data fit to a monomer-dimer model with dimerization dissociation constants of 0.03 μM and 0.20 μM for p150CC1B and NudECC, respectively, indicate that both are strong dimers and that, of the two, p150CC1B is the tighter dimer (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: Both p150CC1B and NudECC unfold with a midpoint temperature between 40 and 50°C.
source: Circular dichroism (CD) spectra acquired at temperatures ranging from 5 to 60°C (Figure 2C) show that both proteins unfold with a midpoint temperature between 40 and 50°C.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CD data in Figure 2C.

claim: The coiled-coil structures of p150CC1B and NudECC are confirmed by their CD spectra which show helical structures and values for 222/208 ratios larger than 1.
source: Also of note, the coiled-coil structures of p150CC1B and NudECC are confirmed by their CD spectra which show helical structures and values for 222/208 ratios larger than 1 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CD data in Figure 2C.

claim: The measured mass of approximately 29.5 kDa for IC1-260 based on MALS data is consistent with the expected mass of 29.2 kDa for an IC1-260 monomer.
source: The measured mass of approximately 29.5 kDa based on the MALS data is consistent with the expected mass of 29.2 kDa for an IC1-260 monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SEC-MALS data in Figure 2D.

claim: Ct IC is unique in including a strongly predicted third helix (H3) corresponding to residues 170-200.
source: Ct IC is unique, however, in also including a strongly predicted third helix (H3) corresponding to residues 170–200 (Buchan and Jones, 2019; Muñoz and Serrano, 1997; Muñoz and Serrano, 1994; Muñoz and Serrano, 1995a; Muñoz and Serrano, 1995b; Nucleic Acids Research, 2021; Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text with supporting citations and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The estimated fractional helicity values for IC constructs at 5°C are in the range of 20-35%, which matches the fraction of predicted helical residues in each construct.
source: The estimated fractional helicity (Wei et al., 2014) values for these constructs at 5°C are in the range of 20–35%, which matches the fraction of predicted helical residues in each construct (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CD data in Figure 3B-E.

claim: IC1-260 is the most thermostable of the four IC constructs tested and resists unfolding until above 50°C.
source: Notably, the longest IC construct (IC1-260) is the most thermostable of the four and resists unfolding until above 50°C.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CD data in Figure 3B.

claim: IC1-88, IC160-240, and IC100-260 exhibit some loss in secondary structure significantly below 50°C.
source: Comparatively, IC1-88, IC160-240, and IC100-260 exhibit some loss in secondary structure significantly below 50°C.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CD data in Figure 3C-E.

claim: IC100-260 appears to be the least stable of the three shorter IC constructs, with complete loss of helical structure around 40°C.
source: In particular, IC100-260 appears to be the least stable of the three, with complete loss of helical structure around 40°C.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CD data in Figure 3D.

claim: Some degree of tertiary contacts may exist only within IC1-260 and underlie the increase in its structural stability and cooperative unfolding.
source: From this, it is reasonable to hypothesize that some degree of tertiary contacts may exist only within IC1-260 and underlie the increase in its structural stability and cooperative unfolding.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the CD data.

claim: Upon addition of IC1-88 at a 1:2 molar ratio (IC100-260:IC1-88), a complex with a sedimentation coefficient of 2 S is formed, indicating a strong interaction between the two constructs.
source: Upon addition of IC1-88 at a 1:2 molar ratio (IC100-260:IC1-88), a complex with a sedimentation coefficient of 2 S is formed, indicating a strong interaction between the two constructs; a peak for the excess of IC88 is not observed because IC1-88 does not absorb at 280 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: SEC-MALS determined a mass of 30.3 kDa for the IC1-88/IC100-260 complex which matches the expected mass of 30.6 kDa for a 1:1 complex.
source: SEC-MALS determined a mass of 30.3 kDa for the IC1-88/IC100-260 complex which matches the expected mass of 30.6 kDa for a 1:1 complex (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SEC-MALS data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Strong tertiary contacts exist within IC1-260.
source: Together, these data confirm the presence of strong tertiary contacts within IC1-260 and explain the increase in its stability compared to smaller IC constructs (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the SV-AUC and SEC-MALS data.

claim: The limited chemical shift dispersion at 10°C, along with appearance of the majority of the peaks in the CLEANEX experiment at this temperature, indicates that the peaks observed in the NMR spectra are for the disordered regions of IC1-260.
source: The limited chemical shift dispersion at 10°C (Figure 4B), along with appearance of the majority of the peaks in the CLEANEX experiment at this temperature (Figure 4C), indicates that the peaks observed in the spectra are for the disordered regions of IC1-260.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 4B-C.

claim: Almost all of the observable peaks in the NMR spectra, corresponding to 37% (90 of 245) of the non-proline residues, were assigned for IC1-260.
source: Using triple resonance experiments on a 2H/13C/15N-labeled sample, we assigned almost all of the observable peaks, corresponding to 37% (90 of 245) of the non-proline residues (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 4B.

claim: The assigned peaks all correspond to residues in disordered linker regions of IC1-260.
source: The assigned peaks all correspond to residues in disordered linker regions of IC1-260, and these peaks vary considerably in intensity (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 4A.

claim: At 40°C, peaks with much greater chemical shift dispersion become visible in the 1H-15N TROSY spectrum of IC1-260.
source: Upon increasing the temperature to 40°C, peaks with much greater chemical shift dispersion become visible in the 1H-15N TROSY spectrum (Figure 4D), while peaks corresponding to disordered regions of the protein disappear.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 4D.

claim: IC1-260 does not undergo significant secondary structural changes in the 10-40°C temperature range based on CD data.
source: Based on CD data (Figure 3B), IC1-260 does not undergo significant secondary structural changes in the 10–40°C temperature range.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CD data in Figure 3B.

claim: The appearance of peaks at elevated temperatures in the NMR spectra is most likely due to an increased rate of molecular tumbling causing peaks from more structured parts of the protein that were too broad to observe at lower temperatures to narrow and become visible.
source: Therefore, the newfound peak dispersion at higher temperature is not due to an increase in secondary structure. Rather, the appearance of peaks at elevated temperatures is most likely due to an increased rate of molecular tumbling causing peaks from more structured parts of the protein that were too broad to observe at lower temperatures to narrow and become visible.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the NMR data.

claim: IC1-260 contains both structured and disordered regions.
source: Together, these spectra support the conclusion that IC1-260 contains both structured and disordered regions, with the most disordered regions resulting in peaks that are most easily assigned by NMR at low temperature.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the NMR data.

claim: The minimal peak disappearances and peak shifts for the spectrum of 15N-labeled IC1-88 upon addition of unlabeled IC160-240 indicate a limited degree of interaction.
source: The minimal peak disappearances and peak shifts for the spectrum of 15N-labeled IC1-88 upon addition of unlabeled IC160-240 indicate a limited degree of interaction (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 5B-C.

claim: When unlabeled IC100-260 is added to 15N-labeled IC1-88, the effects on the NMR spectrum are much more pronounced than with IC160-240.
source: However, when conducting the same experiment with unlabeled IC100-260, the effects were much more pronounced (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Peaks corresponding to residues in the SAH and H2 regions of IC1-88 either lost intensity or disappeared completely upon addition of IC100-260 or IC160-240, while peaks from linker region residues remained largely unaffected.
source: In both cases, peaks corresponding to residues in the SAH and H2 regions of IC1-88 either lost intensity or disappeared completely, while peaks from linker region residues remained largely unaffected, especially those that are near the C-terminus of IC1-88.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 5B-C.

claim: The NMR data rule out a strong interaction between SAH and H3.
source: These data rule out a strong interaction between SAH and H3.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the NMR data.

claim: Upon titration of 15N-labeled IC216-260 with 15N-labeled IC1-88, many of the IC216-260 peaks disappear or shift.
source: Upon titration with 15N-labeled IC1-88, many of the IC216-260 peaks disappear or shift (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 5D-E.

claim: The tertiary contacts within IC1-260 are largely between the SAH/H2 regions and a region that overlaps with the LC7 binding site.
source: From this, we conclude that the tertiary contacts within IC1-260 are largely between the SAH/H2 regions and a region that overlaps with the LC7 binding site.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the NMR data.

claim: The interactions between SAH/H2 and the LC7 binding site appear to be even stronger in the context of the longer disordered chain encompassing the Tctex and LC8 binding sites.
source: We note that these interactions appear to be even stronger in the context of the longer disordered chain encompassing the Tctex and LC8 binding sites based on the more substantial disappearances of peaks from the SAH/H2 regions when 15N-labeled IC1-88 was titrated with unlabeled IC100-260 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 5C.

claim: IC1-88 bound to p150CC1B shows a sedimentation coefficient of 3.7.
source: By SV-AUC, IC1-88 bound to p150CC1B shows a sedimentation coefficient of 3.7, whereas for IC1-88 bound to NudECC the coefficient is only 2.7 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 6A.

claim: IC1-88 bound to NudECC shows a sedimentation coefficient of 2.7.
source: By SV-AUC, IC1-88 bound to p150CC1B shows a sedimentation coefficient of 3.7, whereas for IC1-88 bound to NudECC the coefficient is only 2.7 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 6A.

claim: The difference in sedimentation coefficients between IC1-88/p150CC1B and IC1-88/NudECC complexes suggests that the complex with NudECC is less compact than the complex with p150CC1B.
source: This is surprising considering that the two complexes have similar overall masses and binding stoichiometries and suggests that the complex with NudECC is less compact than the complex with p150CC1B.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the SV-AUC data.

claim: MALS data of the IC1-88/p150CC1B complex gives a mass of 66 kDa, consistent with the mass expected for a p150CC1B dimer and two monomeric IC1-88 chains.
source: MALS data of the IC1-88/p150CC1B complex gives a mass of 66 kDa, consistent with the mass expected for a p150CC1B dimer and two monomeric IC1-88 chains (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) thus eliminating the possibility that the larger sedimentation coefficient can be explained by a larger than anticipated complex mass.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by MALS data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Peaks for residues corresponding to the H2 region of IC37-88 did not disappear upon titration with NudECC, indicating that the IC H2 region does not directly bind to NudECC.
source: When the same types of experiments were done with NudECC, however, peaks for residues corresponding to the H2 region did not disappear upon titration of 15N IC37-88 with NudECC (Figure 6B, top), indicating that the IC H2 region does not directly bind to NudECC whereas this region does directly bind to p150CC1B.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 6B.

claim: The IC H2 region directly binds to p150CC1B.
source: When the same types of experiments were done with NudECC, however, peaks for residues corresponding to the H2 region did not disappear upon titration of 15N IC37-88 with NudECC (Figure 6B, top), indicating that the IC H2 region does not directly bind to NudECC whereas this region does directly bind to p150CC1B.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 6B.

claim: The difference in binding of IC H2 to p150CC1B versus NudECC is confirmed by ITC experiments using IC37-88 that show binding with p150CC1B but no binding with NudECC.
source: This difference in binding is confirmed by ITC experiments using IC37-88 that show binding with p150CC1B but no binding with NudECC (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ITC data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: For both p150CC1B and NudECC, titration into 15N IC1-88 resulted in IC1-88 peaks disappearing for both the SAH and H2.
source: For both p150CC1B and NudECC, titration into 15N IC1-88 resulted in IC1-88 peaks disappearing for both the SAH and H2 (Figure 6B, bottom).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 6B.

claim: The disappearance of IC1-88 peaks for both the SAH and H2 with NudECC can be explained by weak engagement between NudECC and H2 or an interaction between the SAH and H2 that relays the change in correlation time of the SAH region upon binding to NudECC to the H2 region.
source: The disappearance of IC1-88 peaks for both the SAH and H2 with NudECC can be explained by weak engagement between NudECC and H2 or an interaction between the SAH and H2, previously identified by NMR paramagnetic relaxation enhancement experiments (Morgan et al., 2021), that relays the change in correlation time of the SAH region upon binding to NudECC to the H2 region.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the NMR data with a supporting citation.

claim: IC1-88 and NudECC bind with a 1:1 molar ratio from ITC measurements.
source: From ITC measurements, we observe that, like IC1-88 and p150CC1B (Figure 6C, top left), IC1-88 and NudECC bind with a 1:1 molar ratio (Figure 6C, bottom left), which corresponds to one NudECC dimer binding two IC1-88 monomeric chains.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ITC data in Figure 6C.

claim: IC1-88 and NudECC bind with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.3 μM.
source: Data fit to a simple (single-step) binding model gave a dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.3 μM, which is weaker than the nM affinity estimated for IC1-88 biphasic two-step binding to p150CC1B (Loening et al., 2020; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ITC data.

claim: IC1-88 binding to NudECC is weaker than the nM affinity estimated for IC1-88 biphasic two-step binding to p150CC1B.
source: Data fit to a simple (single-step) binding model gave a dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.3 μM, which is weaker than the nM affinity estimated for IC1-88 biphasic two-step binding to p150CC1B (Loening et al., 2020; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a supporting citation.

claim: Binding of IC1-260 to p150CC1B and NudECC is notably different or undetectable when compared to shorter IC constructs.
source: These differences in IC binding are conserved when a somewhat longer IC construct is used (IC1-150, Figure 6C, center), whereas binding to p150CC1B and NudECC is notably different or undetectable when using a construct containing the entire N-IC region (IC1-260, Figure 6C, right).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ITC data in Figure 6C.

claim: The largest sedimentation coefficient was observed for the IC1-260/LC8 complex among IC1-260 binary complexes.
source: The largest sedimentation coefficient was observed for the IC1-260/LC8 complex; for all other complexes, a less dramatic peak shift was seen, an indicator of either weaker binding, a dynamic equilibrium between free and bound states, and/or a shift to a more elongated conformation (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 7A.

claim: For the IC1-260/NudECC complex, no significant change was observed in the SV-AUC data relative to unbound NudECC.
source: For the IC1-260/NudECC complex, no significant change was observed in the SV-AUC data relative to unbound NudECC.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 7A.

claim: The absence of a peak corresponding to free IC for the sample containing IC1-260 and NudECC indicates that some degree of binding takes place.
source: However, the absence of a peak corresponding to free IC for the sample containing IC1-260 and NudECC indicates that some degree of binding takes place.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the SV-AUC data.

claim: Binding of IC1-260 to NudECC is weak and is thus only detected at a high protein concentration.
source: This result along with our ITC (Figure 6C, bottom right) and NMR (Figure 7B, right) data for this complex indicates that binding of IC1-260 to NudECC is weak and is thus only detected at a high protein concentration.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on multiple experimental techniques.

claim: Upon addition of Tctex or LC8 to IC1-260, only a handful of IC1-260 peaks disappear in the NMR spectra and the patterns of disappearances are similar.
source: Upon addition of Tctex or LC8 (Figure 7B, left), only a handful of IC1-260 peaks disappear and the patterns of disappearances are similar, as expected based on the proximity of the Tctex and LC8 binding sites.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 7B.

claim: When either LC7, p150CC1B, or NudECC is added to IC1-260, considerably more peaks disappear in the NMR spectra compared to addition of Tctex or LC8.
source: When either LC7, p150CC1B, or NudECC is added, considerably more peaks disappear in the spectra for 15N-labeled IC1-260 (Figure 7B, right) and, surprisingly, similar patterns of disappearances occur even though the LC7 binding site is at the C-terminus of IC1-260 whereas the p150CC1B and NudECC binding sites are at the N-terminus.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 7B.

claim: Similar patterns of peak disappearances in NMR spectra for LC7, p150CC1B, and NudECC binding to IC1-260 suggest that regions of the N and C-termini of IC1-260 interact in such a way that when one end of IC1-260 is bound it affects the peak intensities of the other end and vice versa.
source: The similar patterns of peak disappearances suggest that regions of the N and C-termini of IC1-260 interact in such a way that when one end of IC1-260 is bound it affects the peak intensities of the other end and vice versa.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the NMR data.

claim: The shape and symmetry of the eluting SEC peak for the dynein subcomplex (IC1-260/Tctex/LC8/LC7) indicate a weaker binding affinity than when either p150CC1B or NudECC was added.
source: The shape and symmetry of the eluting SEC peak for the dynein subcomplex (~140 mL) indicate a weaker binding affinity than when either p150CC1B (~120 mL) or NudECC (~130 mL) was added.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SEC data in Figure 8A.

claim: Each expected subunit was detected by SDS-PAGE of collected fractions, validating successful assembly of the subcomplexes.
source: In all cases, however, each expected subunit was detected by sodium dodecyl sulphate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) of collected fractions (Figure 8B), thus validating successful assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SDS-PAGE data in Figure 8B.

claim: When all dynein light and intermediate chains are present, the fully bound dynein subcomplex sediments as a single peak with a sedimentation coefficient of approximately 5 S.
source: Using SV-AUC, we show that when all dynein light and intermediate chains are present, the fully bound dynein subcomplex sediments as a single peak with a sedimentation coefficient of approximately 5 S (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 8C.

claim: Addition of NudECC to the dynein subcomplex only slightly increases the sedimentation coefficient.
source: Surprisingly, addition of NudECC, which adds approximately 45 kDa of mass, only slightly increases the sedimentation coefficient.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 8C.

claim: Addition of p150CC1B to the dynein subcomplex increases the sedimentation coefficient to approximately 7 S.
source: In contrast, addition of p150CC1B increases the sedimentation coefficient to approximately 7 S.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 8C.

claim: The subcomplex with p150CC1B is more globular/spherical than the other subcomplexes based on frictional coefficient ratios.
source: These values indicate that the subcomplex with p150CC1B is more globular/spherical than the other subcomplexes.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the frictional coefficient data.

claim: Most of the peaks in the disordered regions observed at 10°C for free IC1-260 remain visible in the spectrum of the dynein subcomplex (IC1-260/Tctex/LC8/LC7), indicating that there is still significant disorder in the fully bound complex (153 kDa).
source: NMR spectroscopy indicates that most of the peaks in the disordered regions observed at 10°C for free IC1-260 (Figure 8D) remain visible in the spectrum of the dynein subcomplex (IC1-260/Tctex/LC8/LC7), indicating that there is still significant disorder in the fully bound complex (153 kDa).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 8D.

claim: Comparison of the NMR spectra of free IC1-260 and dynein subcomplex at 40°C shows a drastic disappearance of peaks.
source: In contrast, comparison of the spectra of free IC1-260 and dynein subcomplex at 40°C shows a drastic disappearance of peaks, indicating that the residues corresponding to these peaks have much longer correlation times in the bound state either due to their involvement in binding or due to the overall increase in weight of the entire subcomplex.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by NMR data in Figure 8D.

claim: The estimated mass of 75.4 kDa for ICFL from SEC-MALS matches closely to the expected monomeric mass of 79 kDa.
source: The estimated mass of 75.4 kDa for ICFL from SEC-MALS matches closely to the expected monomeric mass of 79 kDa (Figure 9A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SEC-MALS data in Figure 9A.

claim: Full-length IC is a monomer in solution.
source: This is the first evidence that full-length IC is a monomer in solution and requires the light chains for its dimerization.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding based on SEC-MALS data.

claim: Full-length IC requires the light chains for its dimerization.
source: This is the first evidence that full-length IC is a monomer in solution and requires the light chains for its dimerization.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding based on SEC-MALS data.

claim: ICFL shows a single, homogenous peak with a sedimentation coefficient of 4.0 S by SV-AUC.
source: Furthermore, SV-AUC shows a single, homogenous peak with a sedimentation coefficient of 4.0 S, as would be expected for monomeric ICFL (Figure 9B top).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: Adding either p150CC1B or NudECC to ICFL results in a negligible shift of the ICFL peak in SV-AUC.
source: Adding either p150CC1B or NudECC to ICFL results in a negligible shift of the ICFL peak and, in both cases, show a peak corresponding to unbound p150CC1B or NudECC (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The lack of binding between ICFL and p150CC1B/NudECC shows that autoinhibition occurs in ICFL in a similar manner to what was observed in IC1-260.
source: This lack of binding between ICFL and p150CC1B/NudECC shows that autoinhibition occurs in ICFL in a similar manner to what we have observed in IC1-260.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the SV-AUC data.

claim: ICFL bound to the three light chains (ICFL/Tctex/LC8/LC7) has a sedimentation coefficient of 7.0 S.
source: SV-AUC experiments on the dynein subcomplex show that ICFL bound to the three light chains (ICFL/Tctex/LC8/LC7) has a sedimentation coefficient of 7.0 S but shifts to values of 7.5 and 8 S upon addition of NudECC and p150CC1B, respectively (Figure 9B middle).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The sedimentation coefficient of ICFL/Tctex/LC8/LC7 shifts to 7.5 S upon addition of NudECC.
source: SV-AUC experiments on the dynein subcomplex show that ICFL bound to the three light chains (ICFL/Tctex/LC8/LC7) has a sedimentation coefficient of 7.0 S but shifts to values of 7.5 and 8 S upon addition of NudECC and p150CC1B, respectively (Figure 9B middle).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The sedimentation coefficient of ICFL/Tctex/LC8/LC7 shifts to 8 S upon addition of p150CC1B.
source: SV-AUC experiments on the dynein subcomplex show that ICFL bound to the three light chains (ICFL/Tctex/LC8/LC7) has a sedimentation coefficient of 7.0 S but shifts to values of 7.5 and 8 S upon addition of NudECC and p150CC1B, respectively (Figure 9B middle).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The addition of the light chains allows p150CC1B or NudECC to bind ICFL by relieving IC autoinhibition.
source: These results mimic those seen for IC1-260 and confirm that the addition of the light chains allows p150CC1B or NudECC to bind by relieving IC autoinhibition.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the SV-AUC data.

claim: The ICFL/Tctex/LC8 complex shows a sedimentation coefficient of approximately 5.2 S.
source: The ICFL/Tctex/LC8 and ICFL/LC7 complexes show peaks with sedimentation coefficients of approximately 5.2 and 4.2 S, respectively (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The ICFL/LC7 complex shows a sedimentation coefficient of approximately 4.2 S.
source: The ICFL/Tctex/LC8 and ICFL/LC7 complexes show peaks with sedimentation coefficients of approximately 5.2 and 4.2 S, respectively (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The ICFL/Tctex/LC8 complex exhibits no shift upon the addition of NudECC but does shift to 6.2 S upon the addition of p150CC1B.
source: Interestingly, the ICFL/Tctex/LC8 complex exhibits no shift upon the addition of NudECC but does shift to 6.2 S upon the addition of p150CC1B (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The ICFL/LC7 complex exhibits a shift upon addition of either NudECC or p150CC1B to 4.5 or 5 S, respectively.
source: The ICFL/LC7 complex, on the other hand, exhibits a shift upon addition of either NudECC or p150CC1B to 4.5 or 5 S, respectively (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by SV-AUC data in Figure 9B.

claim: The addition of LC7 is sufficient to allow binding of p150CC1B and NudECC to ICFL.
source: These data suggest that the addition of LC7 is sufficient to allow binding of p150CC1B and NudECC to ICFL, whereas the binding of Tctex and LC8 only promotes p150CC1B binding to ICFL and not NudECC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the SV-AUC data.

claim: The binding of Tctex and LC8 only promotes p150CC1B binding to ICFL and not NudECC.
source: These data suggest that the addition of LC7 is sufficient to allow binding of p150CC1B and NudECC to ICFL, whereas the binding of Tctex and LC8 only promotes p150CC1B binding to ICFL and not NudECC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the SV-AUC data.

claim: Ct IC contains a stretch of about 300 amino acids in the N-terminal domain that are primarily disordered, except for a few short α-helices.
source: N-IC from a variety of species contains a stretch of about 300 amino acids that are primarily disordered, except for a few short α-helices.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of IC.

claim: For Ct IC, the H2 region is disordered and binds directly to p150Glued.
source: Prior work suggests that a more disordered H2 is correlated with tighter IC/p150Glued binding and has shown that, for Ct IC, the H2 region is disordered and binds directly to p150Glued (although mostly in a nonspecific manner) (Loening et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: A more disordered H2 is correlated with tighter IC/p150Glued binding.
source: Prior work suggests that a more disordered H2 is correlated with tighter IC/p150Glued binding and has shown that, for Ct IC, the H2 region is disordered and binds directly to p150Glued (although mostly in a nonspecific manner) (Loening et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to prior work.

claim: The mechanisms at place in IC1-260 remain in the context of the entire IC protein (full-length IC).
source: Furthermore, we demonstrate for the first time, using full-length IC, that the mechanisms at place in IC1-260 remain in the context of the entire IC protein.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding based on experiments with full-length IC.

claim: Free IC1-260 is compact and in an autoinhibited state.
source: Free IC1-260 is compact and in autoinhibited state (Boxed in black), with the single α-helix (SAH), H2, and H3 regions depicted as helices and with colors indicating the LC8 (red), Tctex (orange), and LC7 (yellow) binding sites.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: When LC7 is added to IC1-260, LC7 outcompetes autoinhibition to bind IC1-260, exposing the SAH domain for p150CC1B and NudE binding.
source: When LC7 is added (left arrow) LC7 outcompetes autoinhibition to bind IC1-260, exposing the SAH domain for p150CC1B and NudE binding.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: When p150CC1B or NudECC is added to free IC1-260, autoinhibition prevents NudECC from binding and reduces the binding affinity of p150CC1B.
source: When p150CC1B or NudECC is added (down arrows) to free IC1-260, autoinhibition prevents NudECC from binding and reduces the binding affinity of p150CC1B.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: p150CC1B is able to bind to the H2 region of IC1-260, so binding is not completely prevented by autoinhibition.
source: However, as p150CC1B is able to bind to the H2 region of IC1-260, binding is not completely prevented.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: IC autoinhibition remains in intermediates containing Tctex and/or LC8 based on very limited changes in NMR spectra.
source: Addition of Tctex and/or LC8 (right arrow) leads to a number of possible binary and ternary intermediates. LC8's role of driving IC dimerization is depicted and, in all intermediates, we predict that IC autoinhibition remains based on very limited changes in nuclear magnetic resonance spectra.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: The addition of LC7 leads to formation of the dynein subcomplex and the release of SAH autoinhibition.
source: Continuing to the right, the addition of LC7 leads to formation of the dynein subcomplex and the release of SAH autoinhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: The NudE subcomplex adopts a more elongated conformation based on SV-AUC data.
source: Finally, addition of p150CC1B or NudECC leads to the formation of the p150 and NudE subcomplexes (bottom right). Our sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation data suggest that the NudE subcomplex adopts a more elongated conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: p150CC1B and NudECC have different modes of binding to Ct IC.
source: However, despite their many similarities, p150CC1B and NudECC have different modes of binding to Ct IC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on multiple experimental techniques.

claim: Binding of NudECC induces a more elongated and open conformation of the IC subcomplex while p150CC1B binding results in a more compact conformation.
source: We propose that binding of NudECC induces a more elongated and open conformation of the IC subcomplex while p150CC1B binding results in a more compact conformation as depicted in the model in Figure 10.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed model based on the data.

claim: Autoinhibition is a common regulatory mechanism for dynein as is observed in interactions with the motor domain and dynein activators dynactin and Bicaudal-D1.
source: This is a highly likely possibility since autoinhibition is a common regulatory mechanism for dynein as is observed in interactions with the motor domain and dynein activators dynactin and Bicaudal-D1 (Zhang et al., 2017; Torisawa et al., 2014; Tripathy et al., 2014; Terawaki et al., 2015; Kobayashi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to prior literature.

claim: The disordered linkers in IC allow for the needed flexibility to bring together the SAH region and the C-terminus (200+ amino acids away) and to extend it into an open conformation when LC7 is bound.
source: The disordered linkers allow for the needed flexibility to bring together the SAH region and the C-terminus (200+ amino acids away) and to extend it into an open conformation when LC7 is bound (either on its own, or with the other two light chains), which suggests a unique role for LC7 in regulating IC interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: LC7 has a unique role in regulating IC interactions.
source: The disordered linkers allow for the needed flexibility to bring together the SAH region and the C-terminus (200+ amino acids away) and to extend it into an open conformation when LC7 is bound (either on its own, or with the other two light chains), which suggests a unique role for LC7 in regulating IC interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: The C-terminal end of IC1-260, which contains a portion of the LC7 binding site, interacts with the SAH and results in a closed conformation.
source: The model highlights that the C-terminal end of IC1-260, which contains a portion of the LC7 binding site, interacts with the SAH and results in a closed conformation.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model based on the data.

claim: The closed conformation of IC1-260 is autoinhibitory, preventing binding of the SAH region by p150CC1B or NudECC.
source: The closed conformation is autoinhibitory, preventing binding of the SAH region by p150CC1B or NudECC.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model based on the data.

claim: Residues that overlap with part of the LC7 binding site make the strongest contacts with the SAH, leaving flanking residues to initiate binding to LC7.
source: Our data (Figure 5E) suggest that residues that overlap with part of the LC7 binding site make the strongest contacts with the SAH, leaving flanking residues to initiate binding to LC7 (Figures 5 and 9).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the NMR data.

claim: The overall closed conformation of IC is likely retained by binding of LC8 and/or Tctex since they bind in the center of a long linker.
source: From the limited changes in NMR spectra upon Tctex and LC8 binding, we conclude that the overall closed conformation of IC is likely retained by binding of LC8 and/or Tctex since they bind in the center of a long linker, whereas LC7 binding is required to release the SAH region, thereby allowing assembled IC to fully bind to p150CC1B and NudECC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the NMR data.

claim: LC7 binding is required to release the SAH region, thereby allowing assembled IC to fully bind to p150CC1B and NudECC.
source: From the limited changes in NMR spectra upon Tctex and LC8 binding, we conclude that the overall closed conformation of IC is likely retained by binding of LC8 and/or Tctex since they bind in the center of a long linker, whereas LC7 binding is required to release the SAH region, thereby allowing assembled IC to fully bind to p150CC1B and NudECC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the NMR data.
